entry.content:
This was my latest 48 hour film challange contribution! I had the pleasure of reuniting with Sam Bolton who I worked on The Ketamine film with. It started with us getting toothbrush a prop we had use and 'I can't hear you!' as the line we had to include.

Callum helpfully allowed us use of his street and his bathroom. I recall me ranting about this 'The Toothbrush Man' creature. I kinda wanted him to have a tooth hat like the guards from the film 'The Hogfather'. One very big concern was making sure it didn't look like it was a superhero. It's just The Toothbrush man, like The Mothman or The Lockness Monster.

The Toothbrush Man

entry.title: Squat Whilst You Squat (And Director's Cut)
entry.summary: God, this one was a nightmare. Another result of my film challange, I received the following prompt from Ross McCartan "A man comes home to find a woman is squatting in his home. He tries reasoning with her but she has some outrageous demands. Eventually…
entry.content:
God, this one was a nightmare. Another result of my film challange, I received the following prompt from Ross McCartan "A man comes home to find a woman is squatting in his home. He tries reasoning with her but she has some outrageous demands. Eventually reasoning turns into a conversation and the two seemingly connect until she finally decides to let the man back into his home... Only for her to kick him back out again after they spend the night together."

My dad helped me with the gym idea and very shortly I shipped the script off to the director who was supposed to film it. Weeks went by during the filming segment with the director for this film asking for extra time every week until she asked me to do all the casting and location scouting for her, which I happily obliged. All was going well until  the director was unable to come to set on the day, so I was put in charge. Then it took nearly a year for it to be edited, after which I decided to make my own cut because I was bored. There was also a broken bycycle that none of the cast trusted, which I balanced some camera gear on a road for a few miles.

Squat Whilst You Squat

entry.content:
For his new release 'Charity' I wanted to capture the eerie feeling of his living quaters in Vietnam. Many of the shots involving shadows were based on his own experiences in his dark windowless room. The script was translated into Vietnamese by the talented Phan Quoc Anh. 


Whilst preparing for the shoot, there were a couple of oversights. I left the props to the last minute so he ended up paying through the nose for the mask. 


I also had trouble in his search for string. I traveled to every corner of Ho Chi Minh city in search for string, stopping in and chatting to the proprietors of many craft shops around the city, but was unable to find any string.

I, however, had a stoke of luck! He asked his ever-faithful friend Callum Caddell to hold the mask onto the actor and pretend to be an extra set of arms. 

Charity

entry.title: The Bagel Touch
entry.summary: This was another film birthed from my film challange. For this one, I was in charge of the prompt which was "Two siblings get way too into crumpets, eating far too many. Eventually it bevomrd like that one skittle advert where everything they touch becomes…
entry.content:
This was another film birthed from my film challange. For this one, I was in charge of the prompt which was "Two siblings get way too into crumpets, eating far too many. Eventually it bevomrd like that one skittle advert where everything they touch becomes skittles, except with crumpets. Are they hallucinating this? Are they dying of malnutrition due to eating only crumpets? Will they eat one another? Your choice. Must have a strong emphasis on the colour lavander though. Like king Midas, but with crumpets which grown on things like fungi."

I think the end product carried this rather well except for substituting the crumpets for bagels, which did lessen the squelchy oily vibe I was hoping for. Either way, Alex did a grand job at it.

The Bagel Touch

entry.content:
I have recently starred in the final film (During Uni) of fellow director 'Alex Fletcher'. This film was quite wild, he was brought in last second with many mishaps occuring. A group of freinds is summoned by a magical wizard who wishes to make the boys drink his 'wizard seed', this was very very strange indeed.

The scene where the second wizard arrives was origionally supposed to have a hostage trapped in the boot of the wizard's car. Also, there were little elf hats we were initially supposed to wear but it was unfortunately decided against to the sadness of many people.

One More For The Road

entry.content:
I am a prolific lover of all things Turkish, so it utterly delighted him to finally visit the place. I got by with the small ammount of Turkish I know. 

However, the most exciting thing for me was the pre-arranged meeting with artist 'C.M.Kosemen' author of 'All Tommorows' which I had arranged. We talked for hours whilst Kosemen created art for my family and freinds. 

This was such an amazing city, I wish that I could've stayed there forever.

entry.title: Bye Bye Vietnam!
entry.summary: Finally, after months of misery, I have left Vietnam for good. However I know that there are many things he'll miss. Grab racing, cheap and cool transport, temples everywhere, koi fish cafe's, Iguanas everywhere and the feeling of independance that living in another country gave…
entry.content:
Finally, after months of misery, I have left Vietnam for good. However I know that there are many things he'll miss. Grab racing, cheap and cool transport, temples everywhere, koi fish cafe's, Iguanas everywhere and the feeling of independance that living in another country gave me.

On my last night, I sat outside by the temple and sampled 10 mins of audio recording from by the road for future projects. I also got a sneaky tattoo before I left. 

It was time for m to return home (via Turkey) to all the things I missed: freinds, family, Iceland 3 for £3 deal, Wetherspoons 3 small plates for £13 deal, his pets and of course my camera equipment.
